name: Region monitoring and geofences
plain: Wakes the app when the device enters or leaves a circle: 20 regions on iOS, 100 geofences on Android.
meaning: Lets a retailer know when someone arrives at a store or leaves home. The caps force apps to rotate regions, and the OS keeps them even after the app is closed.

android.persistence: Re-register after reboot, uninstall and reinstall, data clear or Play services data clear
android.note: 100 geofences per app per device user; recommended radius 100 to 150 m; Wi-Fi accuracy 20 to 50 m; background latency 2 to 3 min on average, up to 6 min if stationary

ios.persistence: Persist until stopped or reboot; relaunch after termination; app must recreate the monitor
ios.note: 20 regions or conditions per app; monitoring needs a device unlock after reboot

limits.headline: Can wake the app when you enter or leave set places, up to 20 on iPhone
limits.user_action: You turn on place reminders, home arrival alerts, or a store offer feature, and allow Always location
can: Wake the app when you cross into or out of a circle it set
Send you a reminder when you arrive or leave, even with the app closed
Watch up to 20 places on iPhone, or 100 on Android
cannot: Watch more places than the limit allows
Know your exact route; it only learns that you crossed an edge
Do this without Always location on Android or iPhone
React instantly; Android can take about 2 to 3 minutes, and small circles are less precise
limits.reach_label: Ongoing, but only for set places
limits.differs: iPhone allows 20 regions and may need a device unlock after reboot. Android allows 100 geofences, with a 2 to 3 minute average delay.

story.what_it_is: The phone can wake an app when you enter or leave a map circle, even if the app is closed.

marketing.name: Region monitoring
marketing.pitch: Apple lets apps watch circular areas and be told when you cross them, to power place based features.

marketing.name: Geofencing
marketing.pitch: Google pitches geofencing as a way to react when a device enters or exits an area around a place.

story.for_you: You walk into a store and get a welcome offer, or your home lights come on as you reach your street. It only works if you allow location all the time.
story.for_makers: Makers get a cheap way to react to arrival without draining the battery. Stores, smart home and delivery apps use it, but it can also build a record of the places someone visits.

use_cases.example: Your coffee app pings you with a free pastry offer as you walk near a shop.
Your thermostat starts heating the house when you come within a mile of home.
A grocery pickup app tells the store you have arrived so the order comes out to the car.
A location game wakes up when you reach a real park so a rare creature or event can start.
A gym app checks you in when you walk through the door.
An ad company counts how many people who saw an ad later walked into the store.
A work app clocks field crews in and out when they enter a job site.

risks: Can log sensitive places like clinics
story.android_note: Up to 100 geofences per app. Alerts can lag a few minutes.
story.ios_note: Up to 20 regions per app. It needs Always location access and a phone unlock after restart.

technical_bounds: Needs Always authorization on both platforms
Android geofences are lost at reboot until re-registered

history.change: Region monitoring introduced (later 20 region cap documented)
Background location permission required for geofences

refs.label: Apple: Monitoring the user's proximity to geographic regions
